findings.title: Optional details typed for one person are sent with the next person's deep check
findings.evidence: Rendered FounderPage in a temp RTL test, typed a profile address for Alice Anders/Acme, collapsed More details, ran it, then ran Bob Brown/Zeta. The start bodies were Alice {profileUrl:'linkedin.com/in/alice-anders'} and Bob {profileUrl:'linkedin.com/in/alice-anders'}.
findings.scenario: An investor opens More details, enters Alice's LinkedIn, school and earlier companies, then collapses the panel. Later they check Bob. onSubmit calls keepDetails(Bob, details) with Alice's values, which are hidden from view. Bob's check then uses Alice's profile, school and companies as identity anchors, so Alice's records can be tied to Bob as likely matches.
findings.fix: Reset details to NO_DETAILS whenever qName or qCompany changes (in the router effect at line 232) and after a submit for a different name. Also show a count of the filled details (for example '2 details added') beside the More details button, so hidden values are never sent without the user seeing them.
findings.verifyNote: The details state (founder.js:209) is never reset. The router effect resets name and company only, and onSubmit calls keepDetails(n, c, details) for any new name. A collapsed panel hides Alice's profile and school, which then go out as Bob's identity anchors.
findings.betterFix: In the router effect, when qName or qCompany changes, set details to keptDetails(qName, qCompany) or NO_DETAILS. Do not carry over the previous person's values. Also show a count of the filled details next to the More details button, and open the panel automatically when any detail is set.

findings.title: Green '0 red flags' and a copied memo with no serious matters when every serious record sits under 'If this is the right person'
findings.evidence: redFlagChip({totals:{redFlags:0,ifRightPerson:3}, ifRightPerson:[3 items], screens all clear, assumedCompany:'Acme'}) returned {text:'0 red flags', tone:'chip chip-good'}. summaryChips never reads ifRightPerson. reportText.js never prints report.ifRightPerson. history and list redFlags come from totals.redFlags.
findings.scenario: Someone checks 'Trevor Milton' with no company. The check infers Nikola (identity inferred), so the fraud records go to ifRightPerson and redFlags is empty. The header shows a green '0 red flags', the Red flags card says 'No serious record is tied to this person', and Copy as text gives 'RED FLAGS: None' with no line for the serious matters. Recent checks and the Network Map show 0 red flags.
findings.fix: In redFlagChip, when ifRightPerson has items, return chip-warn with text '0 red flags · N serious if this is the right person', never chip-good. Add an ifRightPerson chip to summaryChips. In the Red flags empty text, point to that block. In reportAsText, add an 'IF THIS IS THE RIGHT PERSON' section. Have listFinishedChecks also return totals.ifRightPerson, and show it in the lists.
findings.verifyNote: Reproduced. With ifRightPerson holding 2 items, no company typed and the screens clear, redFlagChip returns chip-good '0 red flags', because identityNote is null when no company was typed. reportAsText leaves out ifRightPerson, so the copied text says 'None tied'. The jobStore lists carry only totals.redFlags.
findings.betterFix: As proposed. redFlagChip: when ifRightPerson has items, return chip-warn with text '0 red flags · N serious if right person'. Add an IF THIS IS THE RIGHT PERSON section to reportAsText. Have jobStore listFinished and recent also return totals.ifRightPerson, and make the network.js chip amber when it is above zero.

findings.title: Details typed for a common name are dropped when the user picks a person in the chooser
findings.evidence: keepDetails(n, c, details) is stored under the key name|'' when no company is typed. choose(co) pushes company=co, so startDetails = keptDetails(qName, co) reads name|co, which is null, and DeepCheck starts with no details.
findings.scenario: An investor types 'John Smith' with no company and adds a profile address and school, the details that tell namesakes apart. The quick look finds several John Smiths, and the investor clicks 'This one' (Acme). The deep check starts without the profile address or school, which are lost in exactly the ambiguous case they were typed for.
findings.fix: In choose(), copy the kept details to the new key (keepDetails(qName, co, keptDetails(qName, '') || details)), or key the kept details by name only and clear them on a new name.
findings.verifyNote: keepDetails stores the details under the key name|''. choose() pushes company=co, so startDetails reads keptDetails(qName, co), which is null. The deep check never started under name|'' (deepOn is false while choosing), so it starts with no details.
findings.betterFix: In choose(), call keepDetails(qName, co, keptDetails(qName, '') || details) before router.push. Better: have startDetails fall back to keptDetails(qName, '') when the company was picked through the chooser.

findings.title: After 'Run again' on a report opened from Recent checks or the Network Map, a reload shows the old report
findings.evidence: run({fresh:false}) reads the jobId prop (the URL's ?job=) before savedJob/latestJob, and nothing replaces ?job= after a fresh start, so a reload or Back navigation returns the older job.
findings.scenario: An investor opens /founder?name=..&job=A from the Checked chip and clicks Run again. Check B starts and finds a new lawsuit. On a reload (during or after B), the page reads job A and shows A's finished report, without the new red flag, and stops following B.
findings.fix: When a fresh start returns a new jobId, router.replace the URL with job=<new id> (shallow), or pass a callback so founder.js updates qJob. Alternatively, when ?job= is older than latestJob(name, company) for the account, open the newer one and say so.
findings.verifyNote: Nothing in DeepCheck or founder.js rewrites ?job= after run({fresh:true}). On remount, run() reads the jobId prop first, so a reload shows job A's finished report and stops following check B.
findings.betterFix: Add an onJob(id) prop. Once a fresh start returns data.jobId, founder.js calls router.replace with job=id (shallow). Alternatively, prefer savedJob(name, company) over the URL job when the saved one is newer.

findings.title: Quick brief keeps profiles at a different company whose name contains the typed one
findings.evidence: New sameCompany strips spaces and punctuation, then accepts x.includes(y) || y.includes(x): coKey('Rampart Capital')='rampartcapital' includes coKey('Ramp')='ramp'. ownProfiles uses it to decide which profiles are the person's.
findings.scenario: An investor checks 'Eric Glyman', company 'Ramp'. A namesake's profile result, 'Eric Glyman - Partner at Rampart Capital', passes the filter and is listed under Public profiles as his. Its company also feeds NetworkHelpers 'related' companies. Company 'X' or 'Square' matches almost anything ('Exxon', 'Times Square Partners').
findings.fix: Use the shared matcher from utils/network/parseContacts (normalizeCompanyKey with companyMatch or companyFormMatch, whole-word and two-word rule), as network.js now does, instead of a substring test on de-spaced keys.
findings.verifyNote: sameCompany (founder.js:50) does a substring test on keys with spaces removed: 'rampartcapital' contains 'ramp'. ownProfiles uses it to keep profiles that place the person at another company, and a short company name like 'X' matches almost anything. The shared parseContacts matchers (companyMatch, companyFormMatch) exist.
findings.betterFix: Replace it with normalizeCompanyKey plus companyMatch or companyFormMatch from utils/network/parseContacts, which match on whole words, as network.js does.

findings.title: New details typed for a person already checked are silently ignored: the saved check reopens instead
findings.evidence: A new name/company is a non-fresh run, so savedJob, then latestJob, return the existing job and startJob(details) is never called. Only a second submit of the same query (runKey) starts fresh.
findings.scenario: An investor ran 'John Smith / Acme' yesterday and got a thin, namesake-heavy result. Today they come back, open More details, add his LinkedIn and school, and click Run check. The page shows yesterday's report, with nothing saying the details were not used.
findings.fix: In run(), when detailsBody(detailsRef.current) is non-empty and the reopened job's start fields differ (or are absent), either start fresh or show a notice above the report: 'This is the check from <date>; your added details were not used. Run it again with them.' with a button.
findings.verifyNote: For a new query, run({fresh:false}) returns savedJob or latestJob, and startJob, the only call that sends detailsBody, is never reached. Nothing on the page says the typed details were not used.
findings.betterFix: In run(), when detailsBody(detailsRef.current) is non-empty and the reopened job was started without those fields, show a notice: 'This is the check from <date>; your details were not used.' Add a Run again with them button that calls run({fresh:true}).

findings.title: Printing or saving as PDF while a record filter is on prints only the filtered records, with no sign they are filtered
findings.evidence: shownSections = filterRecords(..., filter) does not depend on the printing state. RecordFilters, which carries the only 'Showing 3 of 155' line, is founder-no-print.
findings.scenario: An investor searches the records for 'SEC', then clicks Print or save as PDF for the IC memo. The PDF's record sections hold only the matching records, and nothing in it says the rest were left out.
findings.fix: Ignore the filter while printing (use NO_FILTER when usePrinting() is true), or print a visible line such as 'Filtered: SEC; 3 of 155 records shown' above the sections.
findings.verifyNote: shownSections uses the filter state whatever the printing state, and RecordFilters, the only place that shows the 'shown' count, is founder-no-print. A printed memo silently holds only the filtered records.
findings.betterFix: Use NO_FILTER for shownSections while printing is true (the PrintContext value is available in that component). If a filtered print is wanted, print a line such as 'Filtered: 3 of 155 records shown'.
